newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Crude Outlook - Overhang to weigh on market.
newsitem.headline: Asia Crude Outlook - Overhang to weigh on market.

text.p: Asian crude trading is likely to slow down this week as focus moves to next-month trading, but an overhang of barrels is likely to keep prices under pressure, traders said on Monday.
Most buyers have finished May buying of Middle East grades and both the Indian and Bangchak refinery monthly tenders have been completed.
Philippines oil refiner Petron has issued a tender to buy May loading Qatar Marine or Upper Zakum crude oil.
But traders said that would not necessarily help support the market because most, if not all, spot availabilities of Qatar Marine have already been taken up.
In addition, Upper Zakum rarely trades on a spot basis.
"They might get a term player who wants to resell the crude, but for Qatar Marine they will not get the numbers seen in the market," one trader said.
Qatar Marine slumped to QGPC -50/-45 cents per barrel in spot trading during the past two weeks, amid a wider slump in crude prices because of slow seasonal demand and refinery turnarounds.

But Qatar cut its official selling prices sharply in its latest revision, which will affect March liftings. However, the fact that QGPC cut official prices will support market sentiment over the spot market differential, traders said.
State-owned QGPC cut Qatar Land to Oman plus 40 cents, down 21 cents from Oman plus 61 cents in February. Qatar Marine was cut 27 cents to Oman plus 26 cents from Oman plus 53 cents.
The Petron tender closes later on Monday and offer are valid until early Tuesday.
Oman prices could turn lower again after the crude's differential narrowed late last week to MPM -2 cents from MPM -4/-5 cents.
However, traders said they suspected the discount could widen again to MPM -5/-10 cents, or possible further, unless Stasco -- the major equity player on Oman -- supported the market.
One trader estimated there were still two to three cargoes of Oman for May loading, but no noteable buyers.
Dubai, hit by the absence of buying from India's May tender, was still suffering a May/June contango.
Regional markets were also coming to the end of spot market trading for loadings in April.
Minas and Duri have seen the worst of their recent price slump, traders said, noting deals late last week at flat to the ICP, after earlier trading at ICP -10/-20 cents.
China is maintaining a relatively relaxed buying stance, traders said. It has acquired as much as four very large crude carriers of Cabinda for April loading, which will mostly arrive in May.
The Brent/Dubai has widened out to $1.70/$1.80 for May, as a result of the slide in Dubai, which might curtail some interest in West African purchases.
But alternatively, the Tapis/Brent differential is wide at just under $3.00, making West African imports an attractive alternative for Tapis.
--Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3081)
